result.explanation: This dispute cannot be decided without knowing whether the policy was renewed continuously without any break between January 2020 and June 2026. If the policy was maintained continuously for over 60 months, the moratorium period clause on page 37 prevents the insurer from rejecting the claim for pre-existing conditions or non-disclosure unless fraud is established. Conversely, if there was a lapse in coverage, the 36-month waiting period under the pre-existing disease clause on page 30 could still apply to exclude the claim. Because the records do not confirm whether policy coverage was continuous, a final decision cannot be reached.
result.what_would_change_it: Proof of continuous policy renewals without any break or lapse from January 15, 2020 to June 10, 2026.

arguments.insurer_position: Under the pre-existing disease definition on page 7 and the pre-existing disease clause on page 30, treatment for a pre-existing condition is excluded unless 36 months of continuous coverage have elapsed, and any coverage after 36 months remains subject to the disease having been declared at application and accepted by the insurer. The claimant has not established that the condition leading to the angioplasty was not pre-existing or that it was declared and accepted when applying for the policy. Therefore, coverage cannot be extended under the pre-existing disease terms on page 30 without evidence of prior disclosure and acceptance.
arguments.claimant_position: The policy incepted on 2020-01-15, meaning over six years elapsed before the admission on 2026-06-10, which far exceeds the 36-month waiting period specified in the pre-existing diseases clause on page 30. Furthermore, because the policy has been active for more than sixty continuous months, the claim is protected under the moratorium period clause on page 37 and cannot be contested. The insurer has not established that the condition was a pre-existing disease, nor have they shown any grounds of established fraud or a break in policy coverage.
arguments.insurer_weak_point: Because the policy commenced on January 15, 2020 and the admission occurred on June 10, 2026, more than 60 continuous months of coverage have elapsed, allowing the claimant to invoke the moratorium period clause on page 37 to argue that the claim cannot be contested on pre-existing disease or non-disclosure grounds absent established fraud.
arguments.claimant_weak_point: The insurer may argue that there was an unstated break in continuous policy coverage or assert established fraud to attempt to bypass the moratorium period clause.

result.explanation: The pre-existing diseases exclusion clause on page 30 excludes coverage for pre-existing conditions and their direct complications until 36 months of continuous coverage have elapsed from the policy inception date. With your policy commencing on January 1, 2025, and admission occurring in June 2026, only 17 months of continuous coverage had passed at the time of your angioplasty. Provided the insurer has medical evidence that your cardiac condition was diagnosed or treated prior to policy inception, the rejection under the 36-month waiting period is supported by the policy wording. However, the exclusion cannot stand if the condition arose for the first time after your policy began.
result.what_would_change_it: Medical evidence showing the heart condition was first diagnosed after January 1, 2025, or a policy schedule showing ported prior coverage credits or an opted reduced 12-month waiting period.

arguments.insurer_position: Under the pre-existing disease clause on page 7 and the waiting period clause on page 11, pre-existing conditions and their treatments are excluded from coverage until all mandatory waiting periods are completed. The pre-existing diseases exclusion clause on page 30 mandates a waiting period of 36 months of continuous coverage from the policy inception date before expenses related to pre-existing diseases and their direct complications become payable. Because the policy commenced on January 1, 2025, and the angioplasty took place in June 2026, only 17 months of coverage had elapsed, rendering the claim non-payable under the policy terms.
arguments.claimant_position: If the angioplasty treatment arose from underlying chronic conditions such as high blood pressure or cholesterol, it is covered under the ABCD Chronic Care clause on page 69 after a 30-day waiting period, which was fully satisfied between policy inception on January 1, 2025, and admission in June 2026. Furthermore, if the policyholder transferred prior continuous coverage credits under the portability clause on page 7 or elected a reduced waiting period under the PED waiting period modification clause on page 26, the standard 36-month exclusion period is reduced or waived. Consequently, the insurer cannot summarily reject the claim under the standard pre-existing disease exclusion without accounting for these specific coverage terms.
arguments.insurer_weak_point: The insurer bears the burden of proving that the insured's cardiac condition requiring angioplasty was actually diagnosed, treated, or advised upon prior to policy inception to qualify as a pre-existing disease.
arguments.claimant_weak_point: The insurer may argue that angioplasty is a procedure for coronary artery disease rather than direct management of blood pressure or cholesterol, and that the claimant has provided no evidence of an opted PED modification or ported prior continuous coverage to shorten the 36-month waiting period.
